          Leeds 1-1 Man Utd Stats: Carrick's Men Pegged Back as Winless Run Continues
        
      
                          
                      Oct 18, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
A bruising Premier League encounter captured the imagination at Elland Road, but the teams couldn't be separated. Look back on it with our Leeds vs Man Utd stats page.
Manchester United could have done more to ease the pressure on Michael Carrick at their winless run stretches to six games in all competitions with a 1-1 Premier League draw at Leeds.

After seeing Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancel out Bryan Mbeumo‘s strike, the Red Devils have not won since beating Sabah in their UEFA Champions League opener in early September, while they have also gone five Premier League matches without a win.
And things could have been even worse on Sunday as Leeds had the better chances to win in the second half, with Anton Stach wasting arguably their clearest opportunity.

Though there were no major chances in the opening 25 minutes, there was no shortage of commitment from both sides, with Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel Gudmundsson among those to put in tough early tackles.

Leeds almost drew first blood when Nico Elvedi's downward header from a Stach free-kick was pushed away by Senne Lammens, but Man Utd soon passed up an even bigger chance as Mbeumo headed Youri Tielemans‘ pinpoint cross wide.
Mbeumo made no mistake from Tielemans’ next cross, a low delivery from the right flank in the 35th minute, stretching to guide the ball into the bottom-left corner.

Leeds had a couple of half chances before the interval, but Calvert-Lewin was unable to trouble Lammens with a header and James Justin failed to get enough power behind his shot following a marauding run.
The hosts' pressure paid dividends six minutes into the second half, with Calvert-Lewin well-placed to volley past Lammens after Tarik Muharemovic flicked on Stach's corner.

Ao Tanaka, Noah Okafor and Stach all fired efforts into the stands as Leeds remained in the ascendency, with the latter's chance being the clearest after Diogo Dalot headed the ball straight to him just inside the Man Utd area.

At the other end, Fernandes went close to finding the bottom-left corner, but Carrick's side were lacklustre even after the introduction of Matheus Cunha, and Lukas Nmecha and Stach both had opportunities to win it for Leeds amid a late goalmouth scramble.
United failed to cling on for a morale-boosting victory after Mbeumo put them in front, and that has been something of a theme in the early stages of 2026-27.
Three of Mbeumo's four Premier League goals this season have put Man Utd 1-0 up, with only Erling Haaland (four) boasting more such goals this term.
However, on each of the last three occasions the Cameroonian has given them the lead, United have gone on to draw (also versus Everton and Tottenham).

When Leeds needed a goal, it was no surprise to see Calvert-Lewin step up; he has now scored in six of his last seven home Premier League games (seven goals overall) and boasts eight Premier League goals since the start of April, a figure only Haaland (13) can better in that time.

Furthermore, since Calvert-Lewin's first home game for Leeds last season, his 12 Premier League goals at Elland Road is the third most scored by any player at a particular venue, after Haaland at the Etihad Stadium (19) and Igor Thiago at the Gtech Community Stadium (14).
And after all is said and done, Carrick may be relieved to even leave Yorkshire with a point, after Leeds edged expected goals (xG) by 1.44 to 0.91 – 1.19 of that came in the second half.
